components.text: The quick deduction is a shortcut: 36,000 × (10% − 3%) = 2,520. The example falls in the 10% bracket

footnote: Source: Individual Income Tax Law, Schedule 1, STA Announcement No. 2 of 2024, Annex 1. Each bracket includes its upper limit, not its lower
notes: This is the annual rate table for comprehensive income, seven progressive brackets from 3% to 45%. Read the header first: annual taxable income, what is left after the 60,000 and all deductions. Not salary. Progressive means only the part above 36,000 is taxed at 10%. The first 36,000 is still at 3%. Adding bracket by bracket is tedious, hence the quick deduction. Where does 2,520 come from? Multiplying everything by 10% overcharges the first 36,000 by 7 points, which is 2,520, so you take it back off. Every bracket works the same way. Tonight's example lands in bracket 2, so I have marked it.
